events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph (about 2, average).** It's the best of the four, but expect an average day, not a good one.
- **Fish deep from the boat there.** Start around 100 to 120+ feet of water, and expect to be well out past 120 feet.
- **South Haven is about 1 (below average).** Its last report was also fair at best, with fish around 100 feet on spoons.
- **Grand Haven and Muskegon are about 1 (low confidence).** Neither has a recent report, so I'm working from older reports and past seasons.

## Why

- **St. Joseph ranks first:** The July 5 St. Joseph report rated boat salmon fishing average, with boats fishing well beyond 120 feet (St. Joseph, 2023-07-05).
- **Deep water is the common thread:** The July 5 reports at both St. Joseph and South Haven put the action deep, so I'd expect the fish to stay out past 100 feet this week.
- **Grand Haven and Muskegon are weak picks:** Grand Haven's newest report is 27 days old and Muskegon's is 41 days old. I'd expect them to be no better than average, and the past July reports for both were slow.

## Evidence

**Recent reports**
- St. Joseph, 2023-07-05: boat salmon "decent," quality 2, fish "well beyond 120 feet of water," mixed bag.
- South Haven, 2023-07-05: "fair," quality 1, boats in very deep water, a few fish around 100 feet, most fish on spoons.
- Grand Haven, 2023-06-21 (27 days old): quality 2, salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 65 to 160 feet of water, orange spoons and green or yellow meat rigs.
- Muskegon: no salmon report in the last four weeks. Its latest report is from 2023-06-07.

**Past seasons (similar week, similar buoy temperature around 70 F)**
- St. Joseph, 2022-07-06: quality 1, best water 30 to 40 feet, with flies and Spin Doctors.
- St. Joseph, 2022-07-20: quality 1, a few fish around 100 feet.
- Grand Haven, 2022-07-14: quality 0 (slow), fish 45 to 120 feet down in 100 to 180 feet of water.
- Muskegon, 2022-07-14: quality 0 (slow), best action 45 to 100 feet down.
- South Haven, 2022-07-06: quality 0 (slow).

**Conditions**
- The buoy surface water was warm, about 71 F at St. Joseph and South Haven, and about 68 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon, for the week before today (St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven, Muskegon, 2023-07-18 summary).
- Satellite surface readings near the piers were about 70 to 72 F (satellite, same summary).
- Upwelling wind last week was light: 10 hours at St. Joseph, 4 hours at South Haven, and 11 hours at Grand Haven and Muskegon (same summary). That is not enough to have pulled cold water in.

## Caveats

- **Live conditions were unavailable.** The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before today, not current readings. I haven't seen this week's water or wind.
- **Reports are old.** The newest St. Joseph and South Haven reports are 13 days old. Grand Haven and Muskegon are older still, so those ratings are guesses from past seasons.
- **Lures and depths are thin.** Lures were reported at South Haven only. St. Joseph's July 5 report gave water depth but not fish depth.
- **Expect warm, stratified water.** At about 70 F, I'd expect the fish to hold deep, near the thermocline or below it (general guidance: Michigan Sea Grant, the reference on salmon preferring water of 55 F or less), so check your depth finder.

## Sources

- St. Joseph and South Haven, July 5, 2023: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- Grand Haven, South Haven and St. Joseph, June 21, 2023: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
- Historical comparisons: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31f444a, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31e454b, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/323f6bf
